title: Mukesh Sharma v. State of Haryana
text: The petitioner, Mukesh Sharma, challenges his detention under the National Security Act through a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution. The detention order was not served promptly, and the grounds of detention were vague and did not enable the petitioner to make an effective representation. The right to make a representation is a fundamental right under Article 22(5) of the Constitution. The High Court under Article 226 examines the detention order meticulously. The grounds of detention are found to be stale and do not satisfy the requirements of the National Security Act. The detention order is quashed by a writ of mandamus. The fundamental rights of the petitioner under Articles 21 and 22 have been violated. The respondent-State is directed to release the petitioner forthwith. The court reaffirms that preventive detention statutes must be strictly construed to protect fundamental rights.
